0.0.n: 母 is the usual word for your own mother when speaking to someone outside your family.

0.1.n: が marks 母 as the person who died.

0.2.n: Past form of 死ぬ, describing what happened at the place mentioned next.

0.3.n: 母が死んだ describes 場所 directly: Japanese puts the description before the noun.

0.5.n: This chunk contains 教えて, the connecting form of 教える, plus the beginning of the polite request ending.

0.6.n: This is a fragment of いただけません, expressing a humble request, not the separate word だけ meaning only.

0.7.n: ませ belongs to ません, the polite negative ending within いただけませんか.

0.8.n: ん completes the negative ending ません; the negative question makes the request more courteous.

0.9.n: か turns the polite negative expression into a question asking someone to do you a favor.

1.0.n: This is a place name; 県 identifies it as a prefecture.

1.1.n: の links the prefecture to the village, indicating where the village is located.

1.2.n: 八つ is part of the name 八つ墓村, Yatsuhaka Village, whose literal sense is eight-grave village.

1.3.n: 墓村 is the rest of the name 八つ墓村, not a separate place name; 墓 means grave and 村 means village.

1.4.n: と marks 八つ墓村 as the name being stated.

1.5.n: Polite form of 言う; a name followed by と言います identifies what something is called.

0.lit: The place where my mother died, could I not receive your telling me?
0.tip: 教えていただけませんか is a very polite way to ask someone to tell you something.

1.lit: It is called Yatsuhaka Village of Okayama Prefecture.
1.tip: A name followed by と言います means something or someone is called that name.
